analyst_view.overall: Early view: No. 2 Inter Miami host No. 7 Columbus in Game 1 at Nu Stadium; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. Miami scored 80 league goals and Messi won a second straight Golden Boot, but under Kily Gonzalez they threw away a 3-0 lead against Charlotte on Decision Day, and MLSsoccer.com notes their home record is worse than their away one. Columbus, under interim coach Laurent Courtois, won eight of their last nine (24 goals for, 10 against) and came from behind three times to win 4-3 in Chicago.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals, which is very high, but the news backs it. Miami's last game finished 3-3 and Columbus's 4-3, Miami have the league's most productive attack with Messi and Suarez not called up in November, and Columbus have scored 24 in nine. I stay with the number rather than going higher because playoff openers usually start tighter.

corners.text: The site expects 8.4 corners and I lean lower. Miami won only two corners against Charlotte despite having most of the ball (and scored from both), because they build through Messi and De Paul in the middle rather than crossing; Columbus took four in Chicago. A low count fits both.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, most of them on Miami. Miami committed 14 fouls against Charlotte and Columbus had Tapia and Rodriguez booked in Chicago, which fits the number; with no referee named yet I stay close to it.

shots.text: The site expects 27.3 shots. I lean lower: both teams are efficient rather than high-volume, with Miami scoring three from 11 shots against Charlotte and Columbus four from 11 in Chicago. I expect quality chances rather than a flood of attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Fewer shots does not mean fewer on target here: both Decision Day games had a high share on goal, and Messi, Suarez, Tapia and Brais Mendez rarely waste chances, so I stay with the number.
